coverage: Targeted survey, not systematic or exhaustive; all dates are first preprint submissions.
disclosure: AI-assisted primary-source triage; no independent human review or source-paper reproduction claimed.
confidence_meaning: Subjective confidence in scoping/priority, not calibrated probability of correctness or discovery.

records.title: Escape-Aware Control Barrier Functions for Quadrotor Safety under Body-Rate Limits
records.date_basis: Primary arXiv submission history; preprint, not a verified journal publication date.
records.source_read: Full-text targeted inspection: III-C Proposition 1, IV-C Lemma 1, IV-D Theorem 1 and Remark 2, IV-E.

theorem_or_claim.location: III-C Proposition 1; IV-D Theorem 1 and Remark 2
theorem_or_claim.summary: A directional stopping certificate includes clearance spent reorienting thrust. Theorem 1 concerns existence of an escape maneuver; Remark 2 identifies a thrust-ramp correction and explicitly excludes a recursive-feasibility or forward-invariance conclusion.

assumptions: Fixed obstacle normal during the maneuver; identified reorientation bound; positive aligned braking authority.
Delay pays the angular-budget shortfall under Lemma 1, or use the longer unconditional rotation allowance.
Ramp transient must be bounded explicitly or drift must use current thrust instead of its future endpoint.
failure_modes: Using the future low-thrust endpoint during ramp underestimates inward motion.
Changing obstacle normals or unsupported actuator bounds invalidate the reduced certificate.
records.connection_to_ctrl: Existing backupCBF and safe_decel_max supply an algebraic starting point. A delay-aware certificate must add explicit dynamics assumptions rather than infer robot safety from the existing at-rest implication.
records.proposed_new_question: Can interval-valued state and certified latency bounds be propagated into a transparent rational stopping-distance certificate? This is a proposed synthesis, not a novelty claim.
records.prototype: Independent one-dimensional delayed-braking model with bounded forward acceleration during delay, constant minimum braking afterwards, and exact arithmetic. It does not reproduce the paper's quadrotor theorem.
records.baseline: Instantaneous stopping distance under identical initial states and braking authority.
metrics: sensitivity to delay and speed uncertainty
records.falsifier: One trajectory satisfying every declared bound stops beyond the certified clearance.
records.evidence_tier: T2: primary theorem and caveat inspected; no reproduction
records.novelty_status: Published method; proposed bounded synthesis and formalization only.

confidence.rationale: Direct link to existing stopping math and a small falsifiable prototype; physical-model transfer remains unverified.

records.title: Compute-Constrained Safety Filters with Neuromorphic Event Triggering
records.date_basis: Primary arXiv submission history; submission to ACC 2027 reported, acceptance not established.
records.source_read: Full-text targeted inspection: Assumptions 1-3, III constraint tightening, IV timing architecture, V-B Theorem 2.

theorem_or_claim.summary: A dual event trigger preserves an admissible hybrid-state set and excludes Zeno behavior while an old input remains active until the scheduled application time. Objective suboptimality is allowed; constraint infeasibility is not.

assumptions: Linear plant; bounded disturbance; compact safe set with regular boundary and locally Lipschitz barrier gradient.
Strictly positive uniform feasibility margin; certified residual-growth bounds and threshold inequalities.
Constraint-feasible solver result available within known time T; prescribed application schedule.
failure_modes: Deadline overrun, infeasible iterate, or underestimated growth margin removes the theorem's guarantee.
Computation counts alone do not establish reduced energy or physical safety.
records.connection_to_ctrl: Adds a missing timing contract around algebraic safety kernels and deterministic MPC statements. Existing ISS inequalities may help bound residual growth for a restricted plant.
records.proposed_new_question: Can certified residual growth produce an admissible latency budget for each runtime safety call?
records.prototype: Two-state linear plant with delayed application and logged solver deadlines; compare certificate-predicted deadline limits with adversarial delay sweeps.
records.baseline: Periodic CBF and delay-tightened periodic CBF with the same plant, constraints and deadline distribution.
records.falsifier: A within-contract trajectory violates the barrier or the event trigger misses the latest admissible initiation.
records.evidence_tier: T2: primary theorem and timing assumptions inspected; no reproduction
records.novelty_status: Published method; runtime-contract extraction is a proposed engineering extension.

confidence.rationale: Strong fit to explicit timing assumptions; uniform feasibility and worst-case timing need actual certification.

records.title: VertexCBF: Improving Neural Control Barrier Functions via Vertex-Restricted Control Search
records.date_basis: Primary arXiv v1 and v2 submission history.
records.source_read: Full-text targeted inspection: sections 3-4, Eqs. (6)-(7), Appendix A Eqs. (21)-(27).

theorem_or_claim.summary: The control-affine Hamiltonian maximum over a compact polytope occurs at a vertex. The discrete vertex Bellman expansion has a quantified local first-order consistency bound. Neural training and this consistency calculation do not certify global safety of the learned network.

assumptions: Control-affine plant and compact convex polytope input set.
Appendix A uses a local compact region and a C1,1 smooth test function with a known gradient Lipschitz constant.
failure_modes: Hamiltonian vertex exactness does not make finite-step nonlinear maximization vertex-exact.
A network lying below a geometric constraint may still violate the derivative condition.
Small PDE loss need not select the desired value function.
records.connection_to_ctrl: Convex-combination lemmas already appear in LorentzConeCBF. A separate finite-polytope certificate checker would connect search to the repository's exact-witness principle.
records.proposed_new_question: Can learned candidates propose low-degree polynomial barriers whose derivative conditions are subsequently certified over rational state cells?
records.prototype: Low-dimensional control-affine system; enumerate vertices, export polynomial residual bounds, independently check every cell.
records.baseline: Dense input sampling and an analytic barrier at the same state-grid resolution.
records.falsifier: A derivative violation exists within a cell accepted by the exact checker.
records.evidence_tier: T2: mathematical reduction and consistency argument inspected; learned policy unverified
records.novelty_status: Known convex optimization fact and published method; checker integration remains a proposal.

confidence.rationale: Small exact algebraic core fits ctrl; neural training is not the proof and state-domain verification remains substantial.

records.title: Contraction-Based Model Predictive Control using Bilinear Koopman Realizations with Proportional Error Bounds
records.source_read: Full-text targeted inspection: III-C Assumption 1 and Proposition 1, Theorems 1-2, Algorithm 1, Corollary 2.

theorem_or_claim.summary: Reprojection and relifting keep predictions in physical coordinates. A contraction-based tube with proportional model error supports constraint tightening and recursive feasibility under terminal conditions. The probabilistic claim is over the training dataset.

assumptions: Uniform proportional approximation-error bound, robust contraction metric and feedback satisfying Assumption 1.
Admissible connecting geodesics, terminal ingredients, initial feasibility, and the stated sampling scheme for the high-probability result.
failure_modes: Leaving the certified data region or assuming an unverified contraction metric breaks the guarantee.
A finite-dimensional lifted predictor need not stay on the lifting manifold.
Training-data confidence is not an independently measured per-step failure rate.
records.connection_to_ctrl: MPCFeasibility gives a deterministic shift proof and ISS provides scalar dissipation recurrences. The new obligation is deriving a valid physical error tube, not re-proving the shift under an assumed tube.
records.proposed_new_question: Can a low-dimensional polynomial lifting expose exact certificates for both projection error and contraction?
records.prototype: One nonlinear benchmark with a frozen dictionary, rational local error enclosure, and lifted-vs-relifted rollout ablation.
records.baseline: Nominal Koopman MPC and robust MPC with a constant error bound.
records.falsifier: A state inside the certified domain exceeds the proposed one-step tube bound.
records.evidence_tier: T2: theorem and key assumptions inspected; no reproduction
records.novelty_status: Published method; exact restricted certificate is a proposed extension.

confidence.rationale: Strong library connections but contraction-metric and approximation certificates are major open implementation obligations.

records.title: Adversarially Robust Geometric Safety Certificates for Nonholonomic Robots Against Maneuvering Obstacles
records.date_basis: Primary arXiv submission history, rather than aggregator update date.
records.source_read: Full-text targeted inspection: III-B Remark 4, Theorems 3 and 10, IV-H estimator assumptions, V soft variants.

theorem_or_claim.summary: Contracting barrier geometry gives a conditional invariance statement when robot authority dominates obstacle capability and residual bounds. Single-obstacle boundary feasibility does not establish joint multi-obstacle feasibility.

assumptions: Trajectory stays in the engagement envelope; runtime constraints remain feasible; closed loop is well defined.
Capability and slip bounds plus a strictly positive relative-speed floor.
Estimator coverage additionally assumes capabilities are realized within each observation window at sampling resolution.
failure_modes: Leaving the envelope or approaching zero relative speed removes the certificate.
An adversary can withhold its maximum capability during observation.
Soft barrier variants trade away the strict guarantee.
records.connection_to_ctrl: Useful test of whether new safety statements hide envelope preservation or simultaneous feasibility in their hypotheses. Existing unicycle and algebraic barrier kernels are only starting points.
records.proposed_new_question: Can an explicit runtime contract detect envelope exit and switch to a separately certified backup?
records.prototype: Single-obstacle planar model with adversarial capability switches and a logged validity monitor.
records.baseline: Nominal barrier and derivative-only robustification under the same bounds.
records.falsifier: Within all declared bounds and envelope, a hard-constraint trajectory violates clearance.
records.evidence_tier: T2: conditional theorem and estimator caveat inspected; no reproduction
records.novelty_status: Published method; validity-monitor composition is a proposed question.

confidence.rationale: Good source of falsification cases; assumptions make unrestricted navigation claims inappropriate.

records.title: Imitation Learning of Avoidance Modes for Efficient Multimodal Model Predictive Control
records.source_read: Full-text targeted inspection: sections 3-4, Algorithm 1, section 5.1 evaluation setup.

theorem_or_claim.summary: A learned avoidance-side proposal and a previous-mode candidate limit online optimization to two solves. This is an empirical computational method, not an end-to-end safety theorem.

assumptions: The evaluation observes ego and obstacle states without noise.
Acceptance includes SQP success or residuals below the specified tolerance.
failure_modes: If neither candidate is accepted, Algorithm 1 applies the last-solved input without repair or certified fallback.
Mode-selection errors and obstacle identity mismatches can cause deadlock or infeasibility.
records.connection_to_ctrl: MPCFeasibility assumes an admissible plan is selected. A learned proposer is compatible with that proof only after an independent admissibility check and a valid fallback.
records.proposed_new_question: Can a learned mode proposer reduce compute while every applied action retains a replayable admissibility witness?
records.prototype: Small avoidance-mode benchmark with a separate exact plan checker; reject both failed candidates and invoke an independently validated backup.
records.baseline: Full mode enumeration and previous-mode-only MPC using identical solver tolerances and hardware.
records.falsifier: An applied plan fails the independent admissibility checker, or timing gains vanish with matched hardware.
records.evidence_tier: T1: full-text empirical algorithm inspected; no applicable safety theorem or reproduction
records.novelty_status: Published empirical method; certified proposal-checker composition is a proposed extension.

confidence.rationale: Concrete architecture lesson, but unsafe failure handling must be replaced before safety-oriented use.

records.title: Barrier Functions Against Safety Drift in Shared Control
records.source_read: Full-text targeted inspection: sections 2-3, mismatch bound, Theorems 1-2, section 3.6 proof.

theorem_or_claim.summary: A filter anchored to an unassisted baseline preserves workload and deviation constraints. Joint feasibility follows because zero assistance satisfies all three constraints.

assumptions: Stable linear baseline, bounded reference, compact admissible assistance including zero.
Initial augmented state lies in the safe set; modeled mismatch bounds and barrier conditions hold.
failure_modes: A faulty baseline or unavailable zero-assistance action removes the feasibility argument.
Model-level workload safety does not establish measured human workload or safety of an arbitrary robot.
records.connection_to_ctrl: Observer and ISS modules could support a bounded deviation argument. The useful design principle is an independent reference whose safety metric is not moved by the same assistance being checked.
records.proposed_new_question: Can assistance checks use a frozen reference trajectory while tolerating bounded model mismatch and sensor error?
records.prototype: Linear joint model with injected assistance bias; compare envelopes anchored to actual state and to an independent baseline.
records.baseline: Assistance-adaptive envelope without an independent reference.
records.falsifier: Within declared mismatch bounds, the independent-reference filter allows deviation beyond its certified tube.
records.evidence_tier: T2: theorem and common feasible action inspected; no reproduction
records.novelty_status: Published method; robot-joint adaptation is proposed and unvalidated.

confidence.rationale: Clear shared feasible-action argument and inspectable fault model; human interpretation must stay narrow.

records.title: Control Barrier Functions for Safe Free-Flying Robotic Spacecraft Operations in Tumbling Target Capture
records.date_basis: Primary arXiv v1 and v2 submission history.
records.source_read: Full-text targeted inspection: III subsystem dynamics, IV Eq. (7)-(9) and subsystem QPs, V simulation.

theorem_or_claim.location: Section IV Eq. (7)-(9), IV-B Eq. (27), IV-C
theorem_or_claim.summary: Subsystem safety QPs use upstream filtered commands as known coupling inputs. A 13-degree-of-freedom spacecraft manipulation scenario is evaluated in Basilisk; this is simulation evidence for a modular architecture.

assumptions: Coupling inputs are known in the subsystem drift; smooth barrier functions and the required CBF inequalities are maintained.
Specific translational, attitude and manipulator models; actuator constraints enter the QPs.
failure_modes: Delayed or erroneous upstream commands no longer equal the known coupling inputs.
Individual barrier constraints need not have a common feasible actuator command.
records.connection_to_ctrl: SE3 and manipulator modules offer algebraic building blocks. The missing cross-module obligation is to turn actual coupling error and update rates into explicit robust bounds.
records.proposed_new_question: Can a contract state the largest admissible upstream command age while preserving a downstream barrier?
records.prototype: Two coupled low-dimensional subsystems with command-age injection and an interval coupling bound before attempting a spacecraft model.
records.baseline: Decoupled filters and ideal zero-delay coupling on the same trajectories.
records.falsifier: A coupled trajectory inside the proposed timing/error contract violates a downstream constraint.
records.evidence_tier: T1: primary equations and simulation architecture inspected; no composition proof audit
records.novelty_status: Published architecture; asynchronous contract formalization is proposed.

confidence.rationale: Useful composition target, but faithful high-fidelity reproduction is large and coupling assumptions need careful auditing.

records.title: Reach-Avoid Certificates for Contact-based Stochastic Hybrid Systems
records.source_read: Full-text targeted inspection: II-C Assumptions 1-2, III Definitions 1-2, Theorem 1, Corollary 1 and Lemma 1.

theorem_or_claim.summary: A smooth contact certificate and compatible measurable reset policy yield an infinite-horizon reach-before-unsafe probability bound. Flow and jump conditions are checked on a sublevel corridor; a fallback policy preserves compatibility.

assumptions: Uniform separation or positive-rate relaunch after each guard event; bounded drift/diffusion data.
Twice-differentiable certificate, finite reset expectation, and a declared measurable compatible policy.
All certificate inequalities hold throughout their continuum domains, not just sampled training points.
failure_modes: Near-tangential contact or an incorrect impact distribution invalidates reset assumptions.
An LP fitted at samples is not an independently verified continuum certificate.
Finite successful rollouts cannot establish the infinite-horizon probability claim.
records.connection_to_ctrl: Exact LP or polynomial certificates fit the search-then-check discipline, but the repository's deterministic contact kernels do not themselves establish stochastic reach-avoid properties.
records.proposed_new_question: Can a simple uncertain bounce model export a rational reset-expectation certificate independently checked before controller execution?
records.prototype: One-dimensional bounce with a finite rational reset distribution; first prove the discrete abstraction and explicitly retain the physical-abstraction gap.
records.baseline: Unfiltered reset policy and a policy constrained only by expected one-step progress.
records.falsifier: Exact enumeration of the finite abstraction violates its claimed probability bound, or physical reset samples violate the assumed support.
records.evidence_tier: T2: theorem and reset assumptions inspected; no reproduction
records.novelty_status: Published theorem; restricted certificate implementation is proposed, not a new theorem claim.

confidence.rationale: Strong new physics/mathematics pairing; full stochastic Lean formalization exceeds a first bounded prototype.

records.title: Following a Unique Path: A Fast Certifier Applied to Outlier-Robust Pose Registration
records.date_basis: arXiv submission history, v1; preprint date, not a journal publication date.

source_read.limit: Relevant full-text passages; independent proof and code reproduction not performed.

theorem_or_claim.kind: conditional certificate criterion plus numerical algorithm
theorem_or_claim.summary: Primal feasibility, dual PSD feasibility and zero complementary slackness certify a feasible QCQP candidate globally. CP-Cert searches for certificates in degenerate relaxations. Its implementation admits numerical tolerances; rank tightness is established empirically for tested problems.

assumptions: Exact certificate criterion requires feasible candidate, symmetric data, PSD dual matrix and exact complementarity.
Central-path mechanism assumes the candidate's lift is the central-path limit; rank tightness plus a nonzero constraint RHS is a sufficient condition.
failure_modes: Floating-point PSD tolerance is not an exact proof.
Non-tight relaxations, nonoptimal candidates or ill-conditioned certificates can fail certification.
Optimality for a chosen cost does not establish correct correspondences or physical safety.
records.proposed_new_question: Can a small pose/data-association candidate export a rational dual witness with either exact optimality or a rigorous additive gap?
records.prototype: First implement a tiny rational QCQP certificate replay, including PSD LDLᵀ and equality residual checks; only then attempt pose instances. Keep external search untrusted.
records.baseline: Direct exact enumeration on tiny instances; floating-point solver certificate with identical objective and constraints.
records.falsifier: Any accepted witness with a better feasible enumerated candidate falsifies the checker. If rational reconstruction rarely succeeds or gap bounds are useless, defer geometric scale-up.
records.novelty_status: Known certificate principle; ctrl integration is proposed, broader novelty unreviewed.

confidence.rationale: Primary certificate equations and numerical boundary are explicit; useful prototype is small. Scaling to realistic pose data remains uncertain.

records.title: Fast and Scalable Multi-Agent Distribution Matching via Partitioned Optimal Transport
records.date_basis: arXiv submission history, v1; preprint date.

source_read.limit: Relevant full-text passages; not independently reproduced.

theorem_or_claim.summary: Mass-balanced block couplings are globally feasible; a barycentric contraction and persistent block membership give cycle-wise descent of a surrogate that upper-bounds squared Wasserstein distance. The paper explicitly does not claim monotonicity of the true Wasserstein optimum.

assumptions: Matching source/target block masses.
Previous coupling remains feasible after motion; block membership persists.
Terminal barycentric contraction with 0 ≤ rho < 1.
Restricted transport is reoptimized at cycle boundaries; full control horizon is executed.
failure_modes: Changing blocks breaks the comparison coupling.
Collision avoidance or actuator limits may invalidate contraction.
A descending upper bound can conceal a rising true transport cost.
records.proposed_new_question: Can a certificate retain a useful descent inequality when assignment changes are admitted only after an exact feasibility check?
records.prototype: Rational 4–16 agent instance with explicit coupling; check marginals, barycenter identity and per-cycle descent. Add deliberate block migration as a negative case.
records.baseline: Global assignment under the same dynamics and partitions held fixed; compare a greedy block allocator.
metrics: Surrogate and true transport cost separately
Collision count as separate empirical metric
records.falsifier: Reject the claimed application if collision filtering routinely destroys contraction or if partition costs overwhelm any latency advantage.
records.novelty_status: Source theorem reproduction first; reassignment certificate is a hypothesis, not a novelty claim.

confidence.rationale: Finite sums and quadratic identities fit existing Lean algebra; system-level benefit depends on constraint interaction.

records.title: Do Better Imagined Rollouts Mean Better Robot Control? A Controlled Study of World-Model Evaluation Under Feedback
records.date_basis: arXiv submission history, v1. A third-party page's later update is not used as a paper version date.

source_read.limit: No reproduction; not a mathematical theorem.

theorem_or_claim.summary: In one simulated navigation setup, estimator rankings from measurement-free rollouts differ more from closed-loop rankings than replay rankings. The result is conditional on estimator, controller and sensing schedule; it is not a universal metric for world models.

assumptions: Simulated three-state differential-drive robot with biased odometry and intermittent landmarks.
Primary study uses one path family and pure-pursuit control; principal recurrent models have three training seeds.
failure_modes: Offline sensor-log replay cannot validate changed closed-loop trajectories.
Visual models, different platforms and longer model-based planning may behave differently.
Changing training outage duration alone need not improve closed-loop performance.
records.proposed_new_question: Do ctrl estimator rankings remain stable when sensing cadence, controller bandwidth and disturbance correlation change?
records.prototype: Deterministic seeded estimator benchmark using matched rollout/update schedules, then paired closed-loop trials on one simple dynamics model.
records.baseline: Same estimators, data, dynamics and controller under measurement-free and measurement-matched evaluation.
records.falsifier: If matched evaluation does not improve selection regret on held-out schedules, retain the negative result and avoid claiming a better benchmark.
records.novelty_status: Replication and evaluation extension; no new mathematical result claimed.

confidence.rationale: High confidence in benchmark relevance and source scope; moderate confidence in any positive replication outcome.

records.title: CoSMO: Conformal Semantic Mapping for Open-World Safe Robot Navigation
records.date_basis: arXiv submission history, v1; record reports CoRL 2026 acceptance.

source_read.limit: Relevant full text; source guarantee not independently formalized.

theorem_or_claim.kind: conditional per-step implication and long-run coverage
theorem_or_claim.summary: Coverage of all current neighborhood labels plus worst-case obstacle dilation implies semantic clearance. The online safety bound is long-run and includes delay/drift and conditional-bias penalties. Guarantees apply after relevant labels enter the vocabulary.

assumptions: Post-discovery vocabulary contains every safety-relevant true label.
Reliable obstacle detection, current embeddings throughout the neighborhood, sufficient sensing radius and bounded per-step motion.
Delayed expert labels; bounded score-CDF drift Delta and conditional bias epsilon.
Planner satisfies the current worst-case clearance constraints.
failure_modes: Unknown hazards before discovery and missing detections are outside the guarantee.
Average coverage allows clustered failures.
Label-dependent clearance distances need independent physical justification.
records.proposed_new_question: Can ctrl expose the exact gap between semantic-set coverage, geometric feasibility, and stopping-distance safety?
records.prototype: Grid-world semantic sets with an explicit unknown-label state; prove the deterministic containment implication before testing adaptive calibration.
records.baseline: Geometry-only planner and fixed conservative dilation at matched feasibility rate.
records.falsifier: If coverage holds while motion violates clearance because of sensing delay or geometry mismatch, reject the composition, not merely retune the threshold.
records.novelty_status: Reproduction of a source implication; additional stopping-distance composition is speculative.

confidence.rationale: Clear theorem boundary; practical oracle and perception assumptions materially limit immediate deployment value.

records.title: Minimum Volume Optimal Transport for Multivariate Conformal Prediction
records.date_basis: arXiv submission history, v1; preprint date.

source_read.limit: Relevant full text; implementation and asymptotic proofs not reproduced.

theorem_or_claim.kind: finite-sample marginal coverage; separate asymptotic results
theorem_or_claim.summary: Learning the transport metric independently of calibration preserves marginal coverage under exchangeability and equivariant tie handling. Volume-optimal metric and oracle-region recovery require additional consistency, separation and regularity assumptions.

assumptions: Exchangeable calibration/test observations.
Metric training independent of final calibration and test response.
Permutation-equivariant assignment tie handling.
Asymptotic optimality additionally needs regular transport/objective behavior and consistent fitting.
failure_modes: Calibration leakage invalidates the stated rank argument.
Temporal dependence or distribution shift may break exchangeability.
Marginal coverage is not conditional or trajectory-wide coverage; minimum volume need not minimize control risk.
records.proposed_new_question: For anisotropic position error, is a task-weighted prediction region more useful for a safety margin than one minimizing Euclidean volume?
records.prototype: Two-dimensional sensor residuals with a frozen train/calibration/test split; compare isotropic, covariance-whitened and learned transport sets before adding any controller.
records.baseline: Split-conformal Euclidean balls and covariance ellipsoids; identical nominal coverage.
records.falsifier: Defer if area shrinks but directional safety margins or held-out coverage worsen; no robot-safety claim follows from calibration alone.
records.novelty_status: Paper is general statistics; robotics pairing is proposed and novelty unchecked.

confidence.rationale: Coverage assumptions are explicit, but robotics data usually need dependence-aware calibration and task-specific evaluation.

records.title: Nonlinear parameter-varying embeddings for nonlinear state estimation with application to a two-link robot manipulator
records.date_basis: arXiv submission history, v1; preprint date.

source_read.limit: Printed bound needs interpretation review; source theorem not accepted as a ctrl result.

theorem_or_claim.summary: An LMI observer design uses a quadratic dissipation inequality. The printed final unnormalized L2 bound omits the initial-energy and normalization terms visible in that inequality; this is a review item before reproduction, not an accepted ctrl guarantee.

assumptions: Known bounded scheduling variables; affine known parameter dependence.
Constant output/disturbance matrices; bounded nonlinear derivatives.
Positive definite certificate and positive decay/disturbance scalars; LMI feasible throughout the parameter set.
failure_modes: Unmeasured scheduling state or unbounded derivative regions violate the model.
Discretization and Gaussian-noise simulations do not automatically satisfy a bounded-disturbance theorem.
Initial conditions and state-norm normalization must be explicit.
records.proposed_new_question: Can the observer claim be reconstructed from an explicit finite-horizon energy inequality with every normalization retained?
records.prototype: Start with scalar dynamics and nonzero initial error; derive and check the normalized energy bound. Only after review, attempt a small rational vertex-LMI certificate.
records.baseline: EKF and fixed-gain observer under identical bounded disturbance and sampling assumptions.
records.falsifier: A zero-disturbance nonzero-initial-error case falsifies any claimed zero total error-energy bound. Reject source transcriptions that omit this term.
records.novelty_status: Faithfulness audit and reproduction; no novelty claim.

confidence.rationale: Promising certificate structure, but notation and bound normalization need resolution before a faithful implementation.

records.title: CyclOT: Learning Quadratic Optimal Transport Maps via Synchronized Forward-Backward Interpolants
records.date_basis: arXiv submission history, v1; preprint date.

source_read.limit: Selected full-text passages; no model training or theorem formalization.

theorem_or_claim.summary: Global minimizers approach forward/reverse quadratic Brenier maps as discriminator richness increases and action weight decreases, under explicit approximation assumptions. This is a population, global-minimizer result, not a finite-training guarantee.

assumptions: Absolutely continuous measures on a compact convex set with nonempty interior.
Generator approximation and nested dense discriminator properties.
Minimizers attained; positive source-target Wasserstein distance.
failure_modes: Finite neural optimization need not find global minimizers.
Cycle consistency does not identify physically correct correspondence.
Discrete or singular sensor manifolds need separate treatment.
records.proposed_new_question: Can physically meaningful invariants reject a low-cycle-error but geometrically wrong sensor-domain transport?
records.prototype: Toy two-dimensional paired ground truth withheld during fitting; compare cyclic transport with direct alignment while testing distance/incidence invariants.
records.baseline: Affine calibration and empirical optimal assignment with the same samples.
records.falsifier: If low cycle loss coexists with wrong physical correspondences, reject cycle loss as a correctness certificate.

confidence.rationale: Useful cautionary benchmark; physics connection and tractable proof scope remain weak.

records.title: From plans to maps: Nonlocal regularization of optimal transport
records.date_basis: arXiv submission history, v1; preprint date.

source_read.limit: Relevant full-text passages; no numerical reproduction or independent proof verification.

theorem_or_claim.summary: A sufficiently singular nonlocal kernel forces every finite-energy coupling to be induced by a map. Fractional regularization can allow jump discontinuities; existence on compact Lipschitz manifolds has explicit dimension and exponent restrictions.

assumptions: Compactly supported measures, continuous nonnegative cost, q > 1 and Borel nonnegative kernel.
Kernel integral diverges almost everywhere as specified in equation (12).
Manifold existence result requires target dimension no larger than source and 0 < alpha < 1/q.
failure_modes: A finite truncated grid kernel does not inherit the continuum singularity theorem.
No smoothness or one-to-one physical correspondence follows automatically.
Regularization can favor a wrong correspondence under missing data.
records.proposed_new_question: Can a finite correspondence penalty preserve true depth discontinuities while exposing where a continuum map guarantee stops applying?
records.prototype: Tiny synthetic two-surface point sets; compare fractional-like edge penalties and smooth penalties, reporting discrete behavior only.
records.baseline: Unregularized assignment and local quadratic smoothing at matched data fidelity.
records.falsifier: If apparent improvement disappears with cutoff changes or erases real boundaries, do not pursue a formalization of the continuum theorem for this application.
records.novelty_status: Exploratory numerical hypothesis; no new theorem or application novelty established.

confidence.rationale: Mathematical result is clear; its discrete robotics transfer needs substantial new justification.
